mainEntity.name: How much does an Audi A1 35 TFSI / 1.5 TFSI engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: The cost varies based on the engine's condition, but for the 1.5 TFSI DPCA/DADA codes, prices typically range from £600 for a used unit to £1,500-£2,500 for a reconditioned engine, with fully rebuilt units ranging from £2,500 to £4,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of COD or oil consumption issues in an Audi A1 35 TFSI / 1.5 TFSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cylinder on Demand and oil consumption are known vulnerabilities in the 1.5 TFSI architecture. Noticeable irregular running or rough idling, especially at low speeds. Dashboard warnings for engine management faults or low oil levels. Increased oil top-up frequency between scheduled service intervals.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for most owners, due to the vehicle's strong retained value and the high cost of equivalent new models.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the DPCA and DADA engine codes in the Audi A1 35 TFSI / 1.5 TFSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: They represent sequential or market-specific calibrations of the same 1.5L EA211 Evo turbocharged petrol architecture.

historyTimeline.h2: Audi A1 35 TFSI / 1.5 TFSI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 35 TFSI badge was introduced for the second-generation (GB) Audi A1 facelift, it signified the adoption of the highly efficient 1.5-litre TFSI engine featuring Cylinder on Demand (COD) technology, replacing the older 1.4 TFSI units for improved emissions and fuel economy.

milestones.description: DPCA / DADA (1.5L TFSI, 150hp) introduced for the facelifted GB generation, featuring Cylinder on Demand (COD) and a gasoline particulate filter (GPF) for strict Euro 6d compliance.
Continued production with minor ECU calibrations to further refine the COD system and improve long-term reliability.

commonProblems.h2: Audi A1 35 TFSI / 1.5 TFSI Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Audi A1 35 TFSI / 1.5 TFSI’s EA211 Evo architecture is generally robust and efficient, but high-mileage examples can develop Cylinder on Demand (COD) solenoid issues or minor oil consumption. Rebuilt engines supplied through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Cylinder on Demand (COD) & Oil Consumption - Why the Audi A1 35 TFSI / 1.5 TFSI Runs Irregularly
problems.rootCause: The COD system deactivates two cylinders under light load to save fuel. Over time, the solenoid actuators can wear, and piston rings may allow minor oil passage, leading to irregular running, EML warnings, or increased oil consumption.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: COD solenoid replacement, ECU software update, and PCV system check
repairOptions.longevity: Highly effective for mild oil consumption or irregular running without internal damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The definitive solution if significant oil consumption or COD failure has caused internal wear.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Apply this UK-wide decision framework: - Vehicle worth under ~£5,000: repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit. - Vehicle worth ~£5,000-£8,000: evaluate both; reconditioned is viable if keeping the car 2+ years. - Vehicle worth ~£8,000-£15,000: reconditioned/rebuilt usually justifies the premium via warranty and reliability. - Vehicle worth £15,000+: replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value.
problems.recommendation: If oil consumption is mild, a specialist ECU update and PCV/COD solenoid check is the most cost-effective first step. However, if the engine is burning significant oil or running roughly due to internal wear, a full rebuilt engine is the only safe long-term solution.
